transcript: Copying is done. But one base doesn't match. Special repair proteins scan the new DNA. Like a spell-checker reading a finished essay. Found it. A mismatch. Enzymes cut around the mistake. They remove that piece. Then they fill in the correct bases. Mismatch repair fixes wrong bases after copying is finished. Next up: damage from UV light. Swipe.
